solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pop out with Hogarth print

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone nips out to buy a reproduction of a Hogarth engraving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop out' reads like nipping out, but 'out' is the anagram signal; the painter in the surface steers towards an art print rather than a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A print is a photographic copy made from a negative, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: European could be French

explanation.definitionFit: A Pole is European, with the adjective Polish; French polish is a wood-finishing shellac.

clue.text: Alloy containing gold spy finally replaced by uranium

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: finally replaced by says the spy word's last letter is swapped for the element symbol

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A metal contains gold, and a spy has been swapped for radioactive uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLE loses its final E to U, the symbol for uranium, giving MOLU after OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is a gilded bronze or brass alloy used for decorative mounts.

clue.text: Bother! Undone! Having broken up one may be this

indicators.note: broken up indicates the letters are shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: An exclamation of distress from someone whose relationship has just ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up' is both the anagram signal and the cause of the state the definition describes, which gives the clue its neat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: On the rebound describes someone just out of a relationship, as one may be after a split.

clue.text: Appreciate value of carpet

explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to esteem or appreciate, a rate is a value, and to rate someone is to scold, carpet them.

clue.text: Short video covering new Conservative bill

indicators.note: in a down clue covering means the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: a promo is a short promotional video
Tory is the familiar name for a Conservative

explanation.surface: A brief film about a fresh Tory piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' is not legislation here but a headland, as in Portland Bill on the English coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a narrow promontory, a headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Bar fight

explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a pole or bar on a ship; to spar is to box or argue.

clue.text: Cover surface round top of Ionian column

indicators.note: round means the covering word wraps around the single letter

parts.note: to plaster is to cover a surface

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter, the top in a down clue

explanation.surface: Instructions to coat the capital of an Ionic column.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a rectangular column projecting from a wall.

clue.text: Orbison and top celebrities supporting Queen

parts.note: Roy Orbison was an American singer
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Roy Orbison and famous stars backing the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band but means the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist is someone who supports the monarchy, here the Queen.

clue.text: Line's fake, showing lack of talent

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line
an imitation is a fake or copy

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a poet's line as a forgery, proof of no ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A limitation is a shortcoming or restriction in ability, here a want of talent.

clue.text: Work round old trick

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone works their way around an ancient deception.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning manoeuvre or stratagem, a trick.

clue.text: Dish in kitchen where pins are scattered

parts.note: a bowl is a dish
a galley is a ship's or aircraft's kitchen

explanation.surface: A dish dropped in a kitchen where sewing pins are strewn about.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bowling alley skittle pins are knocked down and scattered.

clue.text: Like peanuts? Full, having consumed pounds

indicators.note: having consumed means the first word swallows the second, holding it inside

parts.note: sated means full up, satisfied
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A diner, stuffed after spending money, reaches for bar snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts are typically sold with salt added, so the question-marked phrase describes them by example.

clue.text: Enormous wastage in fuel

indicators.note: in says the first-named piece goes inside the second

parts.note: coal is a fuel
loss is wastage

explanation.surface: A complaint about the huge amount of fuel being wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means huge, gigantic, a direct synonym of enormous.

clue.text: Ship makes giant wave in seawater

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the salt water

parts.note: brine is salt water, seawater

indicators.note: wave suggests the letters undulate and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vessel creates an enormous wave out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wave' looks like a noun, a giant wave at sea, but works as the anagram signal on the word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Men hunting wild elks arrested

indicators.note: wild indicates the letters run riot and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hunters pursuing wild elk have been taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like a description of the elks, but it rearranges ELKS plus ARRESTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerstalkers are hunters who stalk deer, so they are men out hunting.

clue.text: Draw obtuse angle, rather small

indicators.note: obtuse, meaning dull-witted, signals a muddled arrangement of letters

parts.note: to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A geometry instruction to draw a wide angle that turns out small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtuse' rearranges DRAW into DWAR; 'angle' is not geometry but fishing with rod and line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfish means like a dwarf, small in stature, so somewhat small.

clue.text: Flower border presented in plain language

indicators.note: presented in means the second-named piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: prose is ordinary language, not verse
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A garden flower border described in simple words.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower.

clue.text: Betting about marines willing to be hawkish

indicators.note: about means the first piece is placed around the others

parts.note: wagering is betting
RM stands for Royal Marines
on means willing, as in 'I'm on for it'

explanation.surface: Gambling on whether the marines are ready to take an aggressive line.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmongering describes eagerness to start wars, the stance of a political hawk.

clue.text: Spicy meat unfortunately served up on motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the following piece
in a down clue served up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: alas expresses regret, meaning unfortunately
M1 is Britain's first motorway, read as MI

explanation.surface: A complaint that spicy sausage was dished up at a motorway services.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a major British motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a highly seasoned, spiced cured sausage.

clue.text: Produce new script about model

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a type is a model or example

explanation.surface: Writing a fresh screenplay concerning a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to key text again, producing a new copy of the script.

clue.text: Chewing grass is unusual in insect

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or unusual
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect eating grass would be odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruminant is an animal such as a cow that chews the cud, repeatedly chewing grass.

clue.text: Set of false teeth round a mouth's top

indicators.note: round means the first piece encircles the second

parts.note: a dental plate is a set of false teeth

explanation.surface: Dentures fitting around the roof of a mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The palate is the roof, or upper surface, of the inside of the mouth.

clue.text: Exploits when holding court

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Deeds performed while holding court.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts are deeds or feats, the same sense as exploits used as a noun.

clue.text: I fool someone admired

parts.note: to con is to fool or trick

explanation.surface: A confession of deceiving a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a revered figure, a person greatly admired.

clue.text: Anthology: I flog about 100 in a lot

indicators.note: in says the built piece goes inside the next word's letters

parts.note: many means a lot

indicators.note: about means the selling pieces wrap around the number

parts.note: to flog is slang for to sell
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A bookseller boasts of shifting a hundred volumes of collected writings in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog' means beat in the surface but is slang for sell; 'a lot' looks like an auction lot but gives a word meaning numerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed collection of writings, which is what an anthology is.

clue.text: Notice East European in superior sort of TV

indicators.note: in places the two single letters inside the television abbreviation

parts.note: HD is high definition, a superior picture standard

explanation.surface: Someone spots an Eastern European on a high-definition screen.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to take notice of or pay attention to something.

clue.text: I see my Reds playing here

indicators.note: playing signals that the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Liverpool fan says this is where they watch their red-shirted team play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reds is the nickname of Liverpool FC; Merseyside is the English county around Liverpool, so 'here' is where the speaker watches them.
explanation.definitionFit: The county around Liverpool is home of the Reds, so it is the place the speaker means.
